column1: # Hand-curated classes of Korean lemmas, read by rule conditions (rewrite rules: x.class=NAME). A lemma may be in
# several classes. Members are added by reading cases, never by counting a corpus.
#   class   state: verbs of feeling and remembering whose ている is a state, not an action in progress
#           (覚えてる → 기억해, 疑ってる → 의심해); 알다 and 생각하다 are not (わかってる → 알고 있어,
#           考えてる → 생각하고 있어 read naturally)
#           nonagent: predicates of a change that happens to the subject (passive, -어지다, 되다, -받다)
#           person: nouns for people the dictionaries carry without a person code (후보, 언니, 모두)
#   lemma   the Korean lemma (with 다); ~ending: every lemma with that ending

column3: 떨어지다, 정해지다: a change that happens to the subject (rows with ~ match a lemma ending)
